svg.text: Example 1. A local copy: n records from src to dst in the tile's own big SRAM
REGISTERS.md 7.1 — one stream, mode 2 to the tile itself (d = 0): read through the address generator, back through the loopback, landing at PTR[me]
PTR[me] = dst; // where the records land
DMA_SRAM_REMAINING = n; // n packets to land
eject: every packet for this tile
routes each packet by its mode;
local wake: every counter done → WFI returns
modes 2, 4: at PTR[src]; mode 3: at PTR[bucket digit]; then += 2
mode 4: high 32 bits ← ordinal from DMA_RECORD_BASE_ADDRESS
SRAM read queue: one request a cycle,
a register store: the program's line
a step of the data flow (below)
The start pulse begins the run: the address generator reads STREAM[0] across the table
It makes one read request per record, n in all, into the SRAM read queue at priority 2.
The big SRAM reads the source records, in order.
Each return becomes a mode-2 packet with dst = me (d = 0) and goes to the injection
The router loops it back: dst = me goes straight from injection to eject, never onto the
The traffic director routes mode 2 to the write engine and decrements
The write engine lands the record at PTR[src] = PTR[me], then adds 2: the destination
The write goes through the SRAM write queue into the destination buffer.
The last record written: DMA_SRAM_REMAINING = 0 and mem_idle, so the local wake fires
A local copy is one stream run: the address generator reads, every read return becomes a packet to the tile itself, and the write engine lands it through
PTR[me]. The program only describes the run (1–3), says how many packets to expect (4), starts it (5) and waits (6). Source and destination must not overlap:
one engine run never reads and writes the same buffer.
Source: REGISTERS.md 2.3, 3.3, 3.4; RECIPES.md 0 and 2 (local_run(), local_copy()); spec/machine-spec.md v1.0, §4.1, §4.2, §4.9, §4.12; the tile map is figure 1.3's.
